releases.notes:
# mcinmc 1.0.0

A Minecraft server inside a Minecraft world. The game process holds the
ports, so friends join your singleplayer world on an unmodified
client.

## Which file

- **mcinmc-1.0.0.mrpack** if you want it to work with no setup. Import it
  in Prism Launcher, the Modrinth App or ATLauncher and you get a ready
  instance.
- **mcinmc-1.0.0.jar** if you already run Fabric for 1.21.1. Needs Fabric
  API.

Only the host installs anything. Guests join with a plain vanilla 1.21.1 client
and no mods.

## What it does

**Port 25565 is your world.** Guests are players in it, with mobs,
chests and the Nether, because it's the simulation already running
inside your game.

**Port 25566 is the Table.** A live model of your world at one block for
every four, on a table you fly above. Everyone online is a small figure
wearing their own face. Pick a figure up and put it down to teleport that
player. Place a block on the model to fill the matching region of the
real world. Power a cell with redstone to lock that ground against
everyone but ops.

**Server Signs.** Write `[server]` on a sign with a name under it and
power the sign or its block. A whole separate server boots inside the
same process, with its own world, save folder and port from 25567
upwards. Signal strength sets the player cap, a comparator reads the
player count, and right clicking as a guest sends you there. Cut the
power and it saves and shuts down.

**The Table can show a sign's server,** so one table runs all of them.

## Requirements

Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric Loader, Fabric API. Works in singleplayer and on
a dedicated server. Ports can be moved with `-Dmcinmc.port`,
`-Dmcinmc.tablePort` and `-Dmcinmc.fleetPort`.

## Read this before opening it up

**Guests aren't authenticated.** Anyone who can reach the port can join
under any name, including yours. Give the address only to people you
trust, and don't leave it forwarded to the internet unattended. Only
operators can affect the world from the Table.
